options.text: The badge is a biometric factor because it is personalized
options.explanation: A carried badge is possession evidence.

options.text: PINs are possession factors because they are entered on a keypad
options.explanation: The keypad is an input device; knowing the secret is the factor.

prompt: A company determines why customer data is collected. A hosted service processes it only under the company’s documented instructions. Which role describes the hosted service?

options.text: Data processor
options.explanation: The service processes data on behalf of the decision maker under instructions.

options.text: Data controller
options.explanation: The controller determines the purposes and means of processing.

options.text: Data subject
options.explanation: The subject is the identifiable person the data describes.

options.text: Data protection officer
options.explanation: That role oversees privacy obligations and does not describe the service relationship.

prompt: A project records a residual risk after mitigation. Which TWO entries make follow-up and escalation actionable? Select TWO.

options.text: Named risk owner
options.explanation: Ownership identifies who is accountable for monitoring and disposition.

options.text: A new asset serial number unrelated to the affected service
options.explanation: This does not identify responsibility or an escalation trigger.

options.text: An assertion that mitigation eliminates all uncertainty
options.explanation: Residual risk remains by definition.

options.text: A threshold that triggers review
options.explanation: A defined threshold tells the owner when to reassess or escalate.

options.text: A duplicate copy of the risk description with no date or owner
options.explanation: Duplication does not establish a decision process.

prompt: The audit objective is to establish whether managers reviewed privileged access every quarter for a full year. Which artifact best answers it?

options.text: Dated review decisions and exception follow-up for all four quarters
options.explanation: These records show execution across the entire audit period.

options.text: The current policy requiring a quarterly review
options.explanation: The policy shows control design rather than execution.

options.text: A clean group membership list exported today
options.explanation: One point-in-time snapshot cannot establish four reviews.

options.text: The workflow configuration created before the year began
options.explanation: Configuration shows expected operation, not completed reviews.

prompt: A supplier passed procurement review last year. It now wants to move customer records to a new subprocessor in another country. Which action best addresses the change before transfer?

options.text: Review the new processing scope against the contract and data requirements
options.explanation: The proposed processor and geography change the risk and contractual facts.

options.text: Accept the transfer based on last year’s unchanged assurance report
options.explanation: Its scope may not cover the new arrangement.

options.text: Cancel the contract before examining its change terms
options.explanation: The agreement may specify a suitable authorization and review process.

options.text: Approve after confirming that the supplier still uses encryption
options.explanation: Encryption alone does not resolve scope, rights or residency.

prompt: Three teams completed phishing training. Which measure most directly tracks whether employees alert responders sooner after receiving a simulation?

options.text: Median time from message delivery to the employee report
options.explanation: This measures the timing of the target behavior directly.

options.text: Percentage of employees who opened the learning module
options.explanation: Attendance does not measure reporting speed.

options.text: Number of reports independent of delivery time
options.explanation: A count does not show how quickly staff reported.

options.text: Number of simulated messages delivered
options.explanation: Delivery volume measures exercise size.

prompt: A business moves a sensitive operation to another country midyear. The policy owner says the next annual review is eight months away. What is the best governance response?

options.text: Trigger a policy review for the material change
options.explanation: A change in operating jurisdiction may affect requirements before the annual date.

options.text: Change the review date on the existing policy and close the issue
options.explanation: Changing metadata does not assess the new operation.

options.text: Wait for the annual review even if obligations have changed
options.explanation: A periodic schedule does not address material changes in the meantime.

options.text: Replace all enterprise policies with the provider’s local handbook
options.explanation: Provider guidance does not establish company governance.

prompt: A site is moving to a new TLS key pair. The CA accepts certificate signing requests (CSRs). Which three actions belong in the issuance and deployment process? Select THREE.

options.text: Generate the key pair within the authorized key boundary
options.explanation: The organization can retain custody of the private key while creating a new pair.

options.text: Attach the private key to the CSR sent to the CA
options.explanation: The CA needs the public key and a signed request, not the private key.

options.text: Submit a CSR containing the intended public key and requested name
options.explanation: The CSR binds the key and identifying information for CA validation.

options.text: Publish the private key in the public certificate chain
options.explanation: Clients verify the certificate using public information.

options.text: Verify the issued certificate against the intended name and key pair
options.explanation: This detects a binding or identity error before serving clients.

prompt: A responder sees a burst of account lockouts. Which three observations add direct evidence for a password-spraying hypothesis? Select THREE.

options.text: The file server completed its scheduled backup
options.explanation: A backup timestamp alone does not connect to the sign-in pattern.

options.text: Failures cover dozens of distinct active accounts
options.explanation: Broad account coverage is characteristic of spraying.

options.text: The affected accounts have different assigned mailboxes
options.explanation: Mailbox assignments alone do not show the source or pattern of failures.

options.text: Each account received few attempts within the window
options.explanation: Sparse attempts per account distinguish the pattern from concentrated brute force.

options.text: The same client source appears throughout the authentication failures
options.explanation: A shared source supports correlation, although it does not identify a particular person.

prompt: A lender needs confidentiality for archived records and traffic to its portal, and must limit which fields service staff see. Which three measures map directly to these requirements? Select THREE.

options.text: Encrypt the archive with controlled decryption keys
options.explanation: This protects stored records if the storage is exposed without the keys.

options.text: Require authenticated TLS on portal connections
options.explanation: TLS protects data in transit and authenticates the intended service.

options.text: Publish a checksum alongside every customer file
options.explanation: Hashes detect changes but do not conceal the file.

options.text: Replicate the archive to a second site
options.explanation: Replication supports availability and creates another copy to protect.

options.text: Mask restricted fields in the service staff view
options.explanation: Role-specific display masking limits routine exposure of those fields.

prompt: An incident handler has approval to acquire a powered-off drive. Which three measures best preserve the original and support later verification of the copy? Select THREE.

options.text: Boot the original operating system to confirm the username
options.explanation: Booting may change disk state before acquisition.

options.text: Use a validated write blocker for acquisition
options.explanation: The blocker protects the source from acquisition-system writes.

options.text: Record acquisition details and custody transfers
options.explanation: Documentation connects the evidence to people, times and handling decisions.

options.text: Use matching filenames as the integrity check
options.explanation: Different content can share the same filename.

options.text: Verify the acquired data using a cryptographic digest
options.explanation: A documented digest comparison supports byte-level integrity verification.

prompt: A business owner is defining recovery priorities. Which three measurements describe the business service’s recovery requirements rather than how it performed during the last outage? Select THREE.

options.text: Maximum tolerable downtime
options.explanation: This states the limit the business can tolerate.

options.text: Measured repair time during the last outage
options.explanation: That is observed performance, not a recovery requirement.

options.text: Recovery time objective
options.explanation: RTO states the target time to restore service.

options.text: Recovery point objective
options.explanation: RPO states the tolerated extent of data loss in time.

options.text: Observed time between the last two failures
options.explanation: This describes historical reliability.
